gaps.quote: Fixed tracks and finitely many work tapes are harmless for this count.
gaps.note: The reader knows Turing machines and tapes, but not multi-track tape machines; the page neither explains nor links 'tracks'.

gaps.quote: Moving one digit in a fixed radix takes a bounded number of scans
gaps.note: 'Scan' as a unit of work on a tape is not explained or linked, so the reader cannot tell what is being counted.

gaps.term: cost of moving one digit is bounded in scans
gaps.quote: Moving one digit in a fixed radix takes a bounded number of scans
gaps.note: Asserted without any argument; the reader cannot see why a digit move needs only a bounded number of scans.

gaps.term: interchanging growing fields needs more work
gaps.quote: interchanging fields whose numbers of digits grow needs more work
gaps.note: Claimed as the contrast with digit moves, but the page gives no reason why such interchanges cost more scans or how much more.

gaps.term: scans as the unit of cost
gaps.quote: so the model's scans are the unit of cost
gaps.note: The page defines cost as a count of machine steps, so the reader cannot see how scans become the unit of cost or why this follows from the preceding claims.
